lendGivenPrincipal derives funding payer from msg.sender and internally constructs callback data; no caller-supplied bytes, arbitrary executor, route, delegatecall or backend signature is accepted by this selected ABI. Fixed callbacks verify the expected immutable factory-derived pool/option or fixed position-token caller. Callbacks, multicall and generic native-balance refund/unwrap helpers remain excluded. No new contract-wallet execution/signing scope is introduced.

Lending supplies one configured pair asset in native token units, and mints ERC1155 Short lending position to param.to. token0/token1 must identify a valid factory pair; they are financial asset identifiers, not arbitrary call targets. Strike is a Q128 ratio; maturity and deadline are Unix seconds. Base-denomination conversion floors in this path and position units depend on strike/pair denomination, not a universal 18-decimal share unit. minReturnAmount and deadline are enforced after/before operation atomically.

Payable lender supports existing native-value model only: if selected funding asset is immutable wrapped native and router native balance covers payment, pay wraps it then transfers fixed amount to option pair; otherwise it pulls caller ERC20 using existing allowance. Shared router native balance can be consumed by this branch; do not prefund/rely on public residual balances. Supply exact necessary native value for native funding or zero for ERC20 funding. Excess/incorrect native value is not refunded by lendGivenPrincipal and public refundNatives is deliberately not admitted; native value is not universally zero for this payable method.

withdraw transfers only msg.sender ERC1155 Short position through existing position-token authorization into withdrawer, burns it, and collects matured option assets to param.to. No operator authorization is granted here. Both token output minima and deadline are checked atomically. It returns token0 and/or token1 ERC20 assets; choose recipient that can receive both. Set nonpayable withdrawal native value to zero. Unwrap-to-native shared-balance helper is excluded.

Maturity settlement is not principal protection: borrower default can produce collateral/alternate-asset payout instead of original principal, and principal value can fall. AMM price/interest and core market fee/rounding effects determine positions and proceeds; periphery selected bodies add no separate fee parameter. Factory validity and source binding do not certify any pair asset, reserves, liquidity, maturity availability or payout value. No early-close, full lending/borrowing workflow, automatic conversion, backing or yield assurance is promised.

An overview of what Timeswap is, its key features, and a quick navigation guide ### Timeswap is the first oracleless lending/borrowing protocol. Timeswap enables the creation of money markets for ANY ERC-20 tokens. By design, **all loans in Timeswap are non-liquidatable and fixed-term.** **Timeswap operate entirely without oracles**, and thus bears no oracle manipulation risks, which is highly prevalent in DeFi. **Timeswap's oracle independence allows the creation of lending/borrowing markets for any ERC-20 tokens.** Timeswap is currently live across **Arbitrum, Mantle, Polygon PoS, Polygon zkEVM and Base.** ## Key features of Timeswap: * **Oracleless:** Timeswap works without any oracles by shifting the pricing and risk management process to the users. Benefits of this design include being immune to oracle manipulation attacks and the ability to support lending/borrowing markets for any ERC-20 tokens. * **Permissionless:** Anyone can create markets for any ERC-20 tokens through Timeswap. Additionally, anyone can lend, borrow, and provide liquidity to any existing pools. * **Non-liquidatable loans:** Borrowers in Timeswap enjoy the security of non-liquidatable loans. This means they can borrow against their token holdings without the constant need for active loan management. In the event of failure to repay the loan before maturity, the collateral provided by the borrower will be forfeited. * **Fixed-term:** All lending and borrowing transactions in Timeswap have a pre-defined loan duration (with respect to the pool) and a fixed interest rate (once the lender/borrower opens a position), providing certainty to users. * **Flexible withdrawals:** Despite being fixed-term, users (lenders, borrowers and liquidity providers) can exit from their positions early. However, it's important to note that early withdrawals may incur slippage, which is further explained in the [Deep Dive](/docs/deep-dive/amm.md) section of this documentation. * **Market-driven interest rates:** Interest rates in Timeswap is determined by the free market through a generalised AMM (inspired by Uniswap V2's x\*y=k AMM), no historical data (e.g., utilisation ratio) is stored in the AMM, resulting in unbiased interest rates. * **Isolated markets:** All lending/borrowing pools in Timeswap are isolated from one another, this ensures that each risks are contained within a pool and participants of a pool is not affected by the outcome of another. * **Overcollateralised loans:** Timeswap's design of states and adoption of arbitrage ensures that at any given time and price, borrowers cannot obtain undercollateralised loans. # Lending FAQ

<details>

<summary>Why is Timeswap asking for NFTs approval? Is it safe?</summary>

![](https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/vjT5VfLq6ZSm1Iw-b33ZIDL2UZyjjTbnSHyak1Au1CQtj4tTZyUfX8EoRT_E-ohQoZUj8X_A7wBQxqmt0XthyqfrWQa86-PQto9WZGXxu03Ldi9bh2JwCc3hLSKy9JBgvL7xBJ6xusKLgCMIShF5-Uw)\
**Timeswap represents your loan (both debt and lend) positions as an ERC-1155 NFT.**

**Approving the request as shown in the above screenshot only allows the Timeswap smart contract to access the Timeswap (position) collection; it does not grant access to any of your other NFT collections.**

*In order to close your loan position, the Timeswap smart contract has to access the active NFTs.*

*Additionally, you could revoke access to the request using* [*revoke.cash*](https://revoke.cash/) *upon closing the loan positions.*

</details>

<details>

<summary>Can I use my Timeswap lending position as collateral to borrow against?</summary>

**No, your Timeswap lending position cannot be used as collateral in Timeswap, as your lending position is represented by an ERC-1155 token (and Timeswap only supports ERC-20 and ERC-4626 tokens).**

</details>

<details>

<summary>What is the transition price?</summary>

**Transition price (a.k.a. strike price) is the price point at and beyond which borrowers are expected to default, and the pool (asset) flips.**

*For example, an ETH-USDC pool in which users are using ETH as collateral.*

*When at maturity, market (spot) price > transition price, borrowers will ideally repay their USDC debt (and lenders will receive their USDC principal and interest).*

*Otherwise, borrowers will usually default on their USDC debt and forgo their ETH collateral (lenders will then receive ETH)*

</details>

<details>

<summary>What does maturity mean?</summary>

**As a lender, maturity indicates the time at which you will realise your principal along with the full interest.** 

</details>

<details>

<summary>What happens if I withdraw my lend positions before maturity?</summary>

**Lenders that withdraw early (before maturity) will not receive the full interest. More details in the** [**Deep Dive**](/docs/deep-dive/amm.md) **section.**

*Lenders that withdraw after maturity will receive full interest payment provided all borrowers repaid their debt.*

</details>

<details>

<summary>Is the APR fixed once I open a lending position?</summary>

**Yes, the APR you see on the UI is locked-in upon opening a lend/debt position. There will be no changes to your loan term’s parameters until the pool’s maturity time is reached (the APR you see on the UI -- after opening your position -- reflects the APR for a new lender/borrower).**

</details>

<details>

<summary>Where is the yield coming from?</summary>

**We are a lending/borrowing protocol, as such, the displayed APR is derived  from interest payments.**

*Lenders’ interest payments come from the borrowers who pay interest to borrow against their collateral with no liquidations. In the case that there is a shortfall of borrowing demand, liquidity providers (LP) are the ones paying interest.*

</details>

<details>

<summary>How is the collateral distributed to lenders when a borrower defaults?</summary>

**Lenders will receive the equivalent amount of the forfeited collateral to their locked-in CDP (insurance amount).**

*For example, a lender lending 1,000 USDC to a USDC-ETH pool at a transition price of 1,000 and CDP of 150%.*

*This translates to 1.5 ETH as insurance to the lender.*

*When the market (spot) price < transition price (e.g., ETH trading at 800 USDC), borrowers are expected to default at maturity. The lender then receives 1.5 ETH (i.e., 1,200 USDC) upon maturity given that ETH took a 20% hit relative to the transition price.*

</details>

<details>

<summary>Why are there different approvals for opening and closing a lend position?</summary>

**When opening a lend position, the approval is for your ERC-20 asset to be lent to the pool.**

**When closing a lend position, the approval is for your ERC-1155 token (Bond Token) that represents your receipt for lending to the pool, the Bond Token will be burnt when closing your lending position.**

</details>
